source_text: Non ergo unitate sacramenti rea monstratur infantia, sed veritate iudicii nihil aliud quam innocens approbatur.
pass_a_gloss: Not therefore by unity of the sacrament is infancy shown guilty, but by truth of judgment it is approved nothing other than innocent.
pass_b_english: The unity of the sacrament therefore does not show infancy to be guilty. Rather, a true judgment proves infancy to be nothing but innocent.

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.
Church rites still pure until now, Julian says; keep sacraments not 'mysteries' unless mysterium is the word.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
